title: March 2011 Class Hospital Final Supplementary Exam (Paper 3)
unit: Paper 3: Community Health, Paediatrics, Mental Health, Research, Sociology

sets.title: Set 1: Original Exam Questions
sets.description: The original MCQs from the March 2011 class Hospital Final Supplementary Examination Paper 3 (TNH, sat 8 November 2013, Part A, Q1 to Q20).

questions.text: When preparing for a community diagnosis:

options.C: Work with the community to take health action
options.D: Sample the households that will be interviewed

questions.explanation: Sample the households that will be interviewed (D) is correct because the preparation (planning) stage of a community diagnosis includes deciding the sampling method and selecting the households to be interviewed, together with the tools, the team and the permission. Submitting a preliminary report (A) and giving feedback in population rates (B) are incorrect because they are done after the data have been collected and analysed (dissemination). Working with the community to take health action (C) is incorrect because it is the final step (implementation of the action plan).

questions.text: In comprehensive school health programme:

options.A: A pregnant pupil shall continue with classes for as long as possible
options.B: The learners shall be educated on the rights to vote
options.C: Learners not be subjected to medical examination
options.D: Learners with disabilities shall attend different classes than able bodied learners

questions.explanation: A pregnant pupil shall continue with classes for as long as possible (A) is correct because the Kenya school health and re-entry policies protect the right of a pregnant girl to education, so she stays in school as long as her health allows and returns after delivery. The learners shall be educated on the rights to vote (B) is incorrect because it is not a component of the school health programme. Learners not be subjected to medical examination (C) is incorrect because routine health screening and medical examination are part of the programme. Learners with disabilities attending different classes (D) is incorrect because the policy supports inclusion in the same classes.

questions.text: The hormonal contraceptive that is recommended for a client on Ritonavir is:
questions.explanation: Depot medroxyprogesterone acetate (A) is correct because ritonavir (a boosted protease inhibitor) induces liver enzymes and so lowers the levels of the hormones in combined pills, progestin-only pills and implants, which reduces their effectiveness, while DMPA is not significantly affected and is the hormonal method recommended (together with condoms, or an IUD). Combined oral contraceptive pill (B), progestin-only oral pill (C) and progestin-only implant (D) are incorrect because their effectiveness may be reduced.

questions.text: The most effective communication media that can be used in a semi-literate community include:
questions.explanation: Puppet shows, songs (B) is correct because they are audio-visual and performing media that do not depend on reading ability, they attract and hold attention and can use the local language. Banners, fact sheets (A), newsletters, videos (C) and booklets, posters (D) are incorrect because they depend mainly on written text, so they are less effective in a semi-literate community (videos are visual but need equipment).

questions.text: A child who weighs 70% of normal weight and has no oedema is classified as:
questions.explanation: Underweight (A) is correct because a weight for age of 60 to 80% of the expected weight without oedema is classified as underweight (moderate malnutrition). Marasmus (B) is incorrect because it is a weight of less than 60% without oedema. Kwashiorkor (C) is incorrect because it has oedema with a weight of 60 to 80%. Marasmic kwashiorkor (D) is incorrect because it has oedema with a weight of less than 60%.

questions.text: Predisposing factors to malnutrition in elderly include:

options.A: Living in a community set up

questions.explanation: Difficulty accessing adequate food (C) is correct because poverty, loss of income, immobility and living alone make it hard for older people to buy, cook and obtain enough food. Living in a community set up (A) is incorrect because social support is protective. Reduced motility of alimentary canal (B) is a physiological change of ageing that mainly causes constipation, so it is a weaker answer. Increased metabolism (D) is incorrect because metabolism falls with age. Note: option B is also arguable, so check this item against the marking scheme.

questions.text: The sociologist who believed that we work hard to produce goods and yet we cannot afford the goods is:
questions.explanation: Karl Marx (A) is correct because his conflict theory and the idea of alienation describe workers who produce goods for the owners of capital but cannot afford to buy them because they receive low wages. Auguste Comte (B) is incorrect because he is the father of sociology and of positivism. Herbert Spencer (C) is incorrect because he proposed social Darwinism and the organic analogy. Max Weber (D) is incorrect because he studied bureaucracy and the Protestant ethic.

questions.text: Hormones produced by the kidney include:
questions.explanation: Renin, erythropoietin (A) is correct because the kidney produces renin (from the juxtaglomerular cells), erythropoietin (which stimulates red cell production) and calcitriol (active vitamin D). Aldosterone (B) is incorrect because it is made by the adrenal cortex. Vasopressin, or antidiuretic hormone (B, C, D), is incorrect because it is made by the hypothalamus and released from the posterior pituitary.

questions.text: The following are features of Down Syndrome:

options.A: Depressed nasal bridge, abnormally small chin

questions.explanation: Single transverse palmar crease, microcephaly (C) is correct because the simian crease and a small head (microcephaly or brachycephaly) are two of the typical features of Down syndrome (trisomy 21). Depressed (flat) nasal bridge, abnormally small chin (A), oversized tongue, thin upper lip (B) and small eyes, up-slanting palpebral fissures (D) each combine one recognised feature (flat nasal bridge, protruding tongue, up-slanting fissures) with a feature that is not typical (very small chin, thin upper lip, small eyes). Note: several options are partly correct, so check this item against the marking scheme.

questions.text: According to WHO analgesic ladder, a patient who is experiencing moderate pain may receive the following drugs:
questions.explanation: Ibuprofen, Codeine (C) is correct because step 2 of the WHO ladder (moderate pain) uses a weak opioid such as codeine or tramadol together with a non-opioid (paracetamol or an NSAID such as ibuprofen). Paracetamol and morphine (A) and amitriptyline, morphine (D) are incorrect because morphine, a strong opioid, belongs to step 3 (severe pain). Ibuprofen, amitriptyline (B) is incorrect because it has no opioid for moderate pain (amitriptyline is an adjuvant).

questions.text: The degree to which a research tool measures what it is supposed to measure is referred to as:
questions.explanation: Validity (C) is correct because it is the extent to which an instrument measures the concept that it is intended to measure. Credibility (A) is incorrect because it is the truth value of findings in qualitative research. Consistency (B) and reliability (D) are incorrect because they mean getting the same results on repeated measurement.

questions.text: The subtype of schizophrenia associated with delusions of persecution and grandiosity, hallucinations but intact affect is:
questions.explanation: Paranoid (A) is correct because it is dominated by persecutory and grandiose delusions and auditory hallucinations, with relatively preserved cognition and affect. Catatonic (B) is incorrect because it shows motor abnormalities (stupor, posturing, excitement). Disorganized (C) is incorrect because it shows disorganised speech and behaviour with flat or inappropriate affect. Residual (D) is incorrect because it has only mild negative symptoms after an acute episode.

questions.text: A child who develops peripheral neuropathy while on isoniazid is given Vitamin:
questions.explanation: B6 (C) is correct because isoniazid interferes with the metabolism of pyridoxine, so peripheral neuropathy is treated (and prevented) with pyridoxine (vitamin B6). Vitamin A (A), vitamin C (B) and vitamin B12 (D) are incorrect because they do not reverse isoniazid neuropathy.

questions.text: Baby Musa's birth weight was 3 kgs. The weight at 6 years is estimated to be:
questions.explanation: 18 kgs (D) is correct because a common rule in paediatric nursing is that the birth weight doubles at 5 months, triples at 1 year and quadruples at 2 years (12 kg), and then increases by about 2 to 3 kg per year, so that the weight at 5 years is about 5 times the birth weight and at 6 years about 6 times the birth weight (3 x 6 = 18 kg). 9 kg (A) is the weight at 1 year. 12 kg (B) is the weight at 2 years. 15 kg (C) is the weight at about 5 years. Note: other formulas (such as 2 x age + 8 = 20 kg) give a slightly higher value, so check this item against the marking scheme.

questions.text: Edema in nephritic syndrome is caused by:
questions.explanation: Increased secretion of antidiuretic hormone (C) is correct because in acute nephritic syndrome the glomerular filtration rate falls, and the retention of salt and water (with increased ADH and aldosterone activity) expands the fluid volume and causes oedema (periorbital, hypertension). Decreased secretion of aldosterone (A) is incorrect because aldosterone is increased, not decreased. Increased oncotic pressure (B) is incorrect because it would hold fluid in the vessels and prevent oedema. Decreased hydrostatic pressure (D) is incorrect because the hydrostatic pressure is increased by the fluid overload.

questions.text: The management for a child with hiatus hernia would be:
questions.explanation: Fundoplication (B) is correct because in a child with a hiatus hernia and reflux that does not respond to medical management (thickened feeds, upright positioning, antacids), the surgical repair is a Nissen fundoplication, which wraps the fundus of the stomach around the lower oesophagus. Herniorrhaphy medications (A) is incorrect because the phrase does not describe a treatment. Increased fluid intake with food (C) is incorrect because large volumes worsen reflux. Hernicolectomy (D) is incorrect because it is not a recognised operation for hiatus hernia.

questions.text: A child with status asthmaticus:
questions.explanation: Has not responded to treatment (B) is correct because status asthmaticus is a severe, prolonged asthma attack that does not respond to the usual bronchodilator and corticosteroid treatment. Has a recurrent wheeze (A) is incorrect because it describes asthma in general. Requires emergency intubation (C) is incorrect because intubation is needed only in the most severe cases. Has underlying pneumonia (D) is incorrect because pneumonia is not part of the definition.

questions.text: Poliomyelitis is transmitted through:
questions.explanation: Droplet, Feco-oral (B) is correct because the poliovirus spreads mainly by the faecal-oral route (contaminated water, food and hands) and also by oropharyngeal droplets in the early phase of the infection. Direct contact, droplet (A), feco-oral, fomites (C) and fomite, direct contact (D) are incorrect because they list routes that are not the main modes of spread. Note: the faecal-oral route is the main one, so check this item against the marking scheme.

questions.text: A rapist whose behavior is determined by a combination of sexual and aggressive impulses is:
questions.explanation: Sadistic (C) is correct because in the sadistic rapist sexual arousal and aggression are fused, so the violence itself is erotic and the victim is hurt for sexual gratification. Vindictive (A) is incorrect because the anger rapist uses violence to express hatred or revenge, and the sex is a weapon. Opportunistic (B) is incorrect because the rape is impulsive and takes place during another crime. Non sadistic (D) is incorrect because it does not describe the combination of sexual and aggressive drives.

questions.text: TRUE or FALSE: Appropriate therapy for dehydrated children with severe malnutrition is IV Hartmans 20 mgs/kg for 5 hours.
questions.explanation: False (B) is correct because a dehydrated child with severe acute malnutrition is rehydrated slowly and orally or by nasogastric tube with ReSoMal (5 ml/kg every 30 minutes for the first 2 hours, then 5 to 10 ml/kg per hour), and the intravenous route is used only for shock, with Ringer's lactate (Hartmann's) 15 ml/kg over 1 hour, not 20 mg/kg for 5 hours. Fluids are not given in mg, and fast intravenous rehydration risks heart failure.

questions.text: TRUE or FALSE: A 10 month old who has no HIV test result and whose mother is HIV positive is classified as "Suspected symptomatic HIV infection".
questions.explanation: False (B) is correct because without symptoms or a positive test, a child whose mother is HIV positive and who has not been tested is classified as HIV exposed (needs an HIV test and cotrimoxazole prophylaxis). Suspected symptomatic HIV infection requires a positive antibody test or the presence of defined signs such as oral thrush, pneumonia, or sepsis. Note: check this item against the marking scheme.
